slides.text: I have maintained a 4.99 rating on Uber for four consecutive years, and I was not about to let three guys in ski masks carrying duffel bags of unmarked bills ruin my metrics. When they leaped into my Toyota Camry outside First National Bank yelling, 'DRIVE, BRO, THE SWAT TEAM IS COMING!', I calmly locked the gearshift in park and turned around. 'Good afternoon, gentlemen. Are we riding with Marcus today?'

The guy in the middle pointed a shotgun at my headrest. 'Floor it!' I tapped my laminated sign hanging from the visor. 'I cannot merge into traffic until all passengers are buckled and the open container of nitroglycerin is placed securely in the cupholder. Also, there are complimentary mints in the door pocket and a dual-port charger if your burner phones are low.' Out of sheer bewilderment, all three robbers clicked their seatbelts.

For twenty minutes, I evaded four police helicopters using only legal zipper merges, HOV lane etiquette, and soothing NPR jazz. When I dropped them off at the abandoned warehouse dock, the ringleader wiped a tear under his balaclava. 'That was the smoothest felony of my life, Marcus. Do you take cash tips?' They gave me five stars, the 'Great Conversation' badge, and forty grand in sequential twenties.
